main_text.head: VII Thesis. Ambulare in VIA ad regnum coelorum, omnem vera pietatis profectum in se complectitur.
SECT. VIII.
main_text.p: CHristiana conversatio non ideo toties in Scripturis via dicitur, ut in ea otiosi torpescamus; sed, ut necessario in dies magisque omni conamine ad regnum coeleste contendamus: ut patet Ephes. 2. 10. Nos fi-gmentum Dei sumus, creati in operibus bonis, ut in eis AMBULEMUS: & Rom. 6. 4. Ut in novitate vita AMBULEMUS. Sive igitur modus perveniendi ad vitam aeternam Cursus in stadio, sive Labor in vinea, sive Pugna in arena, aut aliud quid in Scripturis vocetur; est nihilominus Ambulatio in via ad haereditatem coelestem, non nostro, sed Christi merito partam & comparatam, ut Patres supra docuerunt. Recte igitur In Matt-cap. 6.{b} Hilarius; Obedire Deo, est iter ad coelum. Non igitur desperandum est de eo, qui in hac via vitam finiverit: Gloriosissimi enim sunt illi, qui per martyrium, ceu per mare rubrum istuc perrexerint. At Per meritum de condigno eo aspirare, est extra viam iter habere. Porrò, de Metaphora Ambulandi in via (pro ea, quâ excelluit, sapientia & eruditione) graviter & eleganter homines virtutum omnium præce-ptis

page.notes: The running head reads "ANTIDOTUM"; the chapter number "Cap.20" at the top right is left out of the running head. The first "Hilarius" reference mark is printed as a superscript "b" before the word, and the note carries the same mark. "vita" at the end of the Rom. 6. 4 quotation is hard to make out and may be "vitae" [?]. The heading "VII Thesis." is printed in small capitals and may read differently. The final word "præce-ptis" is split across the last two lines of the page, with the "ptis" line set to the right.
